text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Prime Minister Majali says trade deficit is basic economic problem; executive powers are coordinating with trade sector.
- Crown Prince Hassan, ending visit to Rome, says Italy and Jordan have similar views on stumbling Middle East peace process.
- Journalist Union council members say they are suspending resignations over new press restrictions.
- Japan lends Jordan $61 million for human resource projects.
- Head of U.N. organisation helping Palestinian refugees says organisation is broke; pins hope on donor meeting in Amman next month.
- Israel's ambassador to Jordan withdraws his resignation.
AL-DUSTOUR
- Majali meets heads of Islamic Action Front and Moslem Brotherhood to listen to their request for holding exceptional session of parliament.
- Islamic Action Front secretary-general Ishaq Farhan says workers would be granted 50 percent of shares in their factories if his party won power in parliamentary elections.
- Businesses declare war on smokers, advertising jobs only for non-smokers.
AL-ARAB AL-YAUM
- Crown Prince Hassan starts visit to Britain on Wednesday.
- Saudi Arabia and Jordan to discuss renewed supplies of Saudi oil during Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal's visit next month.
- Former ministers say new press law is unconstitutional.
AL-ASWAQ
- U.S. aid to Jordan causes crisis in Israel as Israeli minister resigns.
- Minister of State for Information Mutawae says government will not withdraw new press law.
- Traders call on Majali to cut prices.
- Foreign funds activate cement share trading on Amman bourse.
JORDAN TIMES
- Sit-in to protest new press law ends in arrests, injuries.
- Italian government to swap debt for local projects equity. Italy to advocate Jordan's case with Paris Club creditors after Prince Hassan's visit to Rome.
- Jordanian soldier Ahmed al-Daqamsa who shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls could receive death penalty; military trial next week.
